gallery.filename: USS Los Angeles (CA-135) firing a Regulus I missile on 7 August 1957 (NH 97391).jpg
gallery.title: File:USS Los Angeles (CA-135) firing a Regulus I missile on 7 August 1957 (NH 97391).jpg
gallery.description:
The U.S. Navy heavy cruiser USS Los Angeles (CA-135) firing a SSM-N-8 Regulus I missile, on 7 August 1957. The aircraft carrier USS Ticonderoga (CVA-14) is visible in the right background, the missile test ship USS Norton Sound (AVM-1) is visible behind the crane.
Original caption: "West Coast Cruisers Capable of Nuclear Assault -- A Regulus I boils white smoke from booster charges as it roars away from its launcher aboard the heavy cruiser USS Los Angeles off San Diego. The launch, a routine evaluation 'shoot', was conducted during the time that 600 members of the Institute of Aeronautical Science were embarked aboard the attack carrier USS Ticonderoga (CVA-14), right. The demonstration, which included a 'Terrier' guided missile interception of the Regulus, power exhibition, carrier operations, and a HUK exercise, was highlighted by the Regulus launching. The Terrier was fired at the Regulus from the USS Norton Sound (AVM-1), background, on August 7." (Text quoted from the original photo caption, which was released by Commander, Cruiser-Destroyer Force, U.S. Pacific Fleet, on 9 August 1957.)
categories: Images from the Naval History and Heritage Command

gallery.description: The U.S. Navy heavy cruiser USS Los Angeles (CA-135) underway on 21 March 1951. Los Angeles was recommissioned on 27 January 1951. gallery.filename: USS Bremerton (CA-130) and USS Los Angeles (CA-135) at the Hunters Point Naval Shipyard, San Francisco (USA), 13 February 1948 (NH 97453).jpg
gallery.title: File:USS Bremerton (CA-130) and USS Los Angeles (CA-135) at the Hunters Point Naval Shipyard, San Francisco (USA), 13 February 1948 (NH 97453).jpg
gallery.description: The U.S. Navy heavy cruisers USS Bremerton (CA-130), foreground, and USS Los Angeles (CA-135) are towed from the (then) largest drydock in the United States, at the San Francisco Naval Shipyard, while being prepared for inactivation and addition to the Pacific Reserve Fleet, 13 February 1948. Constructed during the Second World War, the 1100-foot (335.5m) drydock was capable of handling the (then) largest ships afloat. Besides handling these two cruisers at one time, the huge dock had accomodated four attack transports in one operation. The (then) World's largest crane is visible at right. Note many other laid-up ships in the area. Among them, at right, are the attack transports USS Rockwall (APA-230) and USS Bottineau (APA-235). the aircraft carrier USS Intrepid (CV-11) is visible on the far right.

gallery.title: File:USN No.637705 - 4 May 1954 (52576326132).jpg
gallery.artist: Faces of ROK: Korean War Photographs
gallery.description:
"Maj.Gen. Kim Chong Oh, ROK, discusses tactics with RAdm. Thomas C. Ragan, USN, ComCruDiv Five, on board the USS Los Angeles (CA-135) while observing amphibious exercises off the east coast of Korea."
NARA / Courtesy of the National Institute of Korea History.

Uploader's note: MG Kim Jong-oh (김종오, 1921-1966) - CO, ROK 6th Division, 1950; CO, ROK 3rd Division, 1951; CG, ROK 9th Division, 1952; Superintendent, Korean Military Academy, 1952-54; ROK Army Chief of Staff, 1961-63; Joint Chief of Staff, 1963-65; retired as General, 1965.
Note MG Kim's "combat patch" of the ROK 9th Division on his right shoulder. MG Kim was superintendent of the Korean Military Academy at that time.
